newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's "Mr. Yen" says major nations agree on yen.
newsitem.headline: Japan's "Mr. Yen" says major nations agree on yen.

text.p: There is no difference of opinion on foreign exchange levels between Japan, the United States and Germany, the Ministry of Finance's director general of international finance bureau Eisuke Sakakibara said in a television interview on Sunday.

"There is no difference of opinion on currencies between the monetaries authorities of the United States, Japan and Germany," Sakakibara, dubbed "Mr. Yen" for his influence on currency markets, said on the Fuji television network.
He added that Japan and the U.S. are in regular contact with each other and market talk that there may be a difference in the views of the two nations is groundless.
Asked about the reasons for the recent weakness in Japanese stocks and the yen, he said : "There was confusion in those markets due to the fiscal year book-closing period."
He said that the Japanese economy has been performing better than the market thinks, and Japanese people should stop selling out their own markets.

Sakakibara said a schedule for Japan's "Big Bang" deregulation of its markets and economy will be released this summer. He warned the measures will hurt Japan's already ailing banks, causing a "bloodletting" shakeout in the sector.
